KIDS GAMES · GAME RULES · 35 CARDS · AGES 3–8

How to play every game in the deck.

Thirty-five classic children’s games, one short page each: the rules card itself, the three steps printed on it, what you need, and one fresh way to play it tonight. Duck Duck Goose, Hopscotch, Simon Says, Tag, Treasure Hunt and thirty more — the answers to “how do you play that?”, all in one place.

Pick a game ↓Cover first, then every rule card in file order.
HOW THE RULES PAGES WORK

The card is the rules. The page is the grown-up’s quiet answer.

Every rule card in the Kids Games deck does the same three things: names the game, shows children playing it, and prints a HOW TO PLAY panel with three numbered steps and a skill the game quietly practices — Imagine + Move, Stop + Go, Watch + Remember. Each page below shows the card first, quotes its three steps word for word, and adds what the card cannot fit: what to gather before you start, one safety-and-sanity note for grown-ups, and a fresh twist for tomorrow.

These rules pages belong to the school’s Kids Games extra class, where every card also opens a full how-to-play guide written for a kid to follow. The two shelves sit side by side: come here for the rules of a game you are about to play, and visit the class when you want the whole game afternoon laid out in tour order. If your child is working on Sports, Movement & Play — Class 37, these games are its playground cousins.

WHERE THIS SHELF FITS

Two shelves, one game cupboard.

The Kids Games extra class walks the older twenty-six-card deck in tour order — throwing games first, then chasing, table, quiet and acting games, and the sidewalk classics at the end — with a lesson a kid can follow on every page. This shelf adds the newer rule cards beside them, one short rules page per game. And for the classes already on the Learning Path, Class 37 · Sports, Movement & Play teaches forty named sports skills, step by step — these games are what the whole family plays between lessons.

Rules bend at your house. Every version here is the friendly starter version — change the words, shorten the course and stop while it is still fun.
